newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Mediterranee Euro CDs sell fast.
newsitem.headline: Banque Mediterranee Euro CDs sell fast.

text.p: Merrill Lynch reported unprecedented demand on Monday for an issue of two-year Eurodeposit notes by Lebanon's Banque de la Mediterranee.

The issue, marketted at $50 million, was so heavily oversubscribed that it was launched on Monday at $75 million and was then raised to $100 million, Paul Raphael, Managing Director of Merrill Lynch International for Eastern Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told Reuters.
The notes had the lowest pricing of any Lebanese issue to date, he added.

They sold at a spread of 265 basis points over U.S. two-year Treasuries after having been marketed during roadshows at 275-300 bp and launched at 265-270 bp, Raphael said in a telephone interview from London.
The issue has a coupon of 8.75 percent for a yield of 8.93 percent.
"This represents the lowest pricing achieved by any Lebanese issue to date. It's the first Lebanese issue with a coupon below nine percent," Raphael said.

He said 55 percent of the notes went to private banks and retail accounts in Europe and the Middle East, 35 percent to institutional investors in Europe -- mainly Germany, Switzerland and France -- and 10 percent to Gulf institutional investors.
Raphael called the demand "amazing" and said it indicated increased investor confidence in Lebanon.
